findings.message: getConversation and listConversations read `pending` but never read `chat.conversation.decided`. A confirmed or cancelled card comes back from History as open, with Add it / Cancel, or as expired. listConversations also counts decided cards older than CARD_DAYS as 'expired action'. Fix: select `decided` and map each card to its decision: confirmed, cancelled, unknown, or open only when undecided. Count only undecided cards as expired, and add a variant test for confirmed, cancelled and undecided cards.
findings.scenario: Confirm 'Pause Audit chain check', then reopen that chat from History → the card shows 'Add it' as if nothing happened. After CARD_DAYS the History row shows '1 expired action' for a write that already ran.

findings.message: findSchedule falls back to `all.filter(title === want).at(0)`. For per-entity schedules that share a title, it quietly picks whichever comes first, so the confirm card names a schedule without its entity and the write lands on an arbitrary one. Fix: if more than one schedule matches the title, throw an invalid_input error that lists the 'Title, Entity' labels to choose from.
findings.scenario: Two entities each have 'Payroll reminder'. The model calls set_schedule_enabled {schedule:'Payroll reminder', enabled:false} → the first entity's schedule is paused, and the card never said which one.

findings.message: `await step("ok")` sits inside the try after the tool has run. If writing the trace step fails, the catch records a second step with outcome 'error' and rethrows. A write that committed is then reported to chat or MCP as a failure, and the trace says it failed. Fix: keep only tool.run inside the try, and record the ok step outside it, so a trace-write failure can't turn a committed write into an error.
findings.scenario: set_schedule_enabled commits, then the trace insert fails → the caller gets an error and the trace shows tool_call outcome=error, but the schedule is paused.

findings.message: The export now puts three write-once objects one after another, with no check for objects that already exist. If a later put fails, the job's retry puts the audit object again and hits ObjectLockedError. The trace and ai-call objects for that day are then never written. Fix: skip a key that already exists with the same body (or treat ObjectLockedError on an identical body as done), and write the core.audit.export row only after all three objects are written.
findings.scenario: The S3 put of trace/<tenant>/2026/10/16.ndjson fails once → retry → the audit object put throws ObjectLockedError on every attempt → that day's trace and ai.call are never exported.

findings.message: policyPatch accepts any string for dataRegion, aiRegion, dbRegion, storageRegion and providerRegion. The old form only allowed REGIONS codes, and a model now fills these fields. Unknown codes are stored and shown as if valid. Fix: validate the four region fields with z.enum(Object.keys(REGIONS)).nullable().optional(), and give providerRegion its own allow-list or format check.
findings.scenario: set_ai_policy {dataRegion:'Sydney'} → stored, and the AI page reads 'Your data stays in Sydney.' with no rejection.

findings.message: When the current expiry has already passed, rotate_secret quietly sets expiresAt to null, so the new credential never expires. The prompt and card say 'keep its expiry', and the hub and Expiring tickets will never flag this credential again. Fix: if the old expiry is past and no new expiresAt is given, refuse with invalid_input and ask for a new expiry.
findings.scenario: An expired Azure DevOps PAT is rotated through 'Ask to rotate' → the new credential has expiresAt null → it never appears under 'Expiring in 30 days'.

findings.message: The Settings hub's Audit card ignores whether the chains verify. It always shows an info chip and never sets `attention`, so a broken audit or trace chain doesn't come first on a hub built to lead with what needs attention. Fix: read the cached auditStatus and raise a bad-tone attention when audit.ok or trace.ok is false.
findings.scenario: A superuser edits core.trace_event and 'Verify now' reports 'Chain broken at event 1' → the hub still says 'Nothing needs you right now.' and the Audit card shows 'N today'.

findings.message: Moving revokeClient and savePolicy onto defineService fixes only the cases that were named. `append` now also writes title and pins to chat.conversation with a raw update: no audit and no permission check (AGENTS rule 5). issueCode, exchangeToken/mint and revokeToken (outside this diff) are still unaudited too. Fix: route the conversation writes through a service (or record why they are exempt), and cover every write path from the earlier finding.
findings.scenario: A chat turn changes a conversation's pins and title → core.audit_event gets no row for that write.

findings.message: The admin pages gate on rolesOf(viewer).includes('Admin'), which follows View as. The admin tools run with viewer.actualRoles and permission checks. The two can disagree: an Admin viewing as an Engineer gets a 404 on the page, yet chat still runs the admin writes. Use one rule, the same permission check, in both places.
The removed KeyForm offered 'Revoke now'. The page now offers only rotate and add chips, with no 'Ask to revoke' chip for revoke_secret. Add one in the row next to 'Ask to rotate'.
revokeMcpClient validates userId only as z.string().min(1). A value that isn't a UUID reaches the uuid column and fails as a Postgres error instead of a clear invalid_input. Use z.uuid().

The 047, 049 and 048 sections aren't closed: the 047 confirm card's div and section and the 049 and 048 sections lack closing tags. Sections 049, 048 and 050 end up nested inside the admin-only 047 section, so the role filter hides 'Chat history' (data-roles=all) from non-Admins. The module standard also says the mock is read-only during a build. Close the tags, and move mock edits into their own change.

USAGE_SOURCES maps only chat, agent and job. Model calls with source ui, mcp or pipeline are counted in the totals but missing from bySource and from the Source filter, so the 'Chat $x, agents $y, jobs $z' note doesn't add up to the Cost ticket. Add an 'other' bucket or map every Source.

confirmAction appends the immutable 'decided: confirmed' trace step before confirmCard checks for replay, cancellation, expiry or a missing secret. The trace then records a confirm that never took effect, one step per retry. Cancel, by contrast, records its step only after it succeeds. Fix: record the decided step with its real outcome (confirmed, expired, already cancelled, failed) after confirmCard settles, or put an outcome in its detail.
findings.scenario: Maya clicks 'Add it' on an expired card, which is refused with decision 'expired'. Or she submits a secret card with no value. The Audit and trace timeline still shows 'Confirmed by Maya' for that trace.

findings.message: Each module's tool card pins `settings_overview {area:'integrations'}`. That read tool returns the hub's Integrations status card, not this module's tool list, so the pin doesn't resolve to the record shown. The Events card on /settings/audit (page.tsx) has no PinButton at all. Fix: pin a read tool that returns the module's tools (for example list_mcp_tools {module}), and add a search_audit pin with the current filter to the Events card.
findings.scenario: An Admin pins the 'delivery' tools card and asks 'which of these are write tools?'. Chat receives the hub area summary (tool count and client count), not delivery's tools.

findings.message: The 047, 049 and 048 mock sections are never closed: the confirm-card div and each `</section>` are missing. 049, 048 and 050 end up nested inside 047, so showing or hiding sections by data-change breaks. The mock is also edited inside this build, although the module standard requires mock changes to go through their own small change. Fix: close each section, and move the mock edits into their own proposal.
findings.scenario: Opening #050-immutable-trace while the 047 section is hidden renders nothing, because 050 is a child of 047.

findings.message: The 'New conversation' dock button still has its own inline reset, separate from the new newChat(). It doesn't close History or clear fields.current, so the two resets can drift apart. Fix: call newChat from the button.
findings.scenario: With History open, pressing the dock's New conversation button clears the log but leaves the History panel covering it.

findings.message: getConversation doesn't exclude archived conversations, although listConversations does. openChat can reopen an archived chat and chatTurn will keep appending to it. Fix: filter `archived_at is null` in getConversation, or refuse new turns on an archived chat.
findings.scenario: A chat archived with archive_conversation is opened by id, continued, and still never appears in History.
